questions.stem_latex: John believes that the best cordial is made from using the ratio 2:6 for syrup to water.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Julie consumed 200 mL of cordial that John made from Question 8(a). Afterwards, she thought that it was too sweet. She then added 300 mL of water to the cordial that John made. The new cordial was perfect for her. What is the ratio of syrup to water that Julie likes? Write your ratio in simplest form.

solutions.latex: At $t = 2$, the diver reached a maximum height of 9 m.
At $t = 4$, the diver is 5 m above the pool.

solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: initial equation; 1: value of $k$; 1: final answer

solutions.latex:
$2\text{ cm} \to 10\text{ m}$ (width); $10\text{ cm} \to 50\text{ m}$ (length).

Capacity $= 10 \times 50 \times 2 = 1000\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ KL}$.

$2:6 \to 1:3$. Total parts $= 4$, and $4$ parts $= 1200\text{ mL}$, so $1$ part $= 300\text{ mL}$.

Syrup : water $= 300 : 900$ (mL).
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct amounts of syrup and water

solutions.latex:
200 mL removed, so 1000 mL remaining. $1000\text{ mL} : 4$ parts, so $1$ part $= 250\text{ mL}$.

Original cordial: syrup : water $= 250 : 750$ (mL).

New cordial: $+300\text{ mL}$ water, so $250 : 1050 = 5 : 21$.

notes: File holds two copies of the paper: pages 0-10 the Mathematics Standard 2 question paper (45 min) and pages 11-21 a Mathematics Standard version with handwritten teacher worked solutions and marking comments (1 hour). Questions are taken from the first copy; solutions from the annotated copy (wordings differ slightly, e.g. 2(a)). No sections or MCQ; Section II assigned to all questions. Typos/issues: (1) Q2(b) printed 'Graph the equations of the revenue and income' but the equations are cost and income (Q2(a) asks for cost); fix: 'cost and income'. The annotated copy's Q2(a) says 'revenue (R)' and its answer R = 20 + 5n is the cost equation; stored as C = 20 + 5n. (2) Q4(d) handwritten solution concludes n = 5 years although its own working shows P(5) = 497.664 < 500 and P(6) > 500; the correct answer is arguably 6 years (t > about 5.03 years); solution stored as printed, needs checking. (3) Q5(d) solution gives only t = 4, though x = 5 also at t = 0 (start); 'after starting' makes t = 4 reasonable. (4) Q2(d) in the original has a lined answer space only. Q5 table is stored as a table with blank x row. Solution figures are cropped from the annotated copy.
